purpose: Field-level vendor ground truth for PhysioPS P&S Reports 4.0 output, for regression testing an independent ANS report engine. Every value is what the vendor printed or stored - no derived, imputed or invented values.
rules: No value in this file was computed by the extractor; every number is transcribed from vendor output or read byte-exact from the .ans binary.
Missing vendor values are null with an explicit reason. null NEVER means zero.
Values with partially occluded glyphs in the vendor bar graphics are marked confidence=low with the reading note preserved.
Patient names and DOB are removed; Case 01..11 identifiers are used. The private mapping lives in ans-vendor-oracle-private-mapping.json.
No HumanOS code or production system was read, executed or modified while producing this artifact.

extraction_method.main_pdfs: Vendor PDFs contain no text layer (pdfplumber/pdftotext return empty). Pages were rendered at 200 dpi with pdftoppm and read visually page-by-page; tesseract OCR of the same renders was used as an independent cross-check. Where the two disagreed, the visual reading was kept and OCR error noted.
extraction_method.report_pdf: Same rendering pipeline; narrative text additionally OCR-extracted.
extraction_method.legacy_doc: Converted with LibreOffice to .docx and to markdown with pandoc; text read directly.

source_class_definitions.ans_direct: The value (or a string/timestamp containing it) is stored byte-exact in the .ans binary.
source_class_definitions.ans_derivable: The value is not stored, but the underlying signal/series needed to compute it is in the .ans binary.
source_class_definitions.pdf_only: The value exists only in the vendor report layer (classification, reference range, layout, axis, window choice).
source_class_definitions.report_pdf_only: Only in the -Report.pdf (Diagnostic Implication Summary / Therapy Options).
source_class_definitions.legacy_doc_only: Only in the legacy .doc clinician letter.

ans_binary_layout.epoch: LabVIEW absolute time = seconds since 1904-01-01 UTC (f64 for timestamps, u32 for DOB)
sequence: [str] name field 1, [str] name field 2, [str] middle (empty in all 11)
[str] gender, [str] physician, [str] ANS medications, [u32] empty, [u32] age
[str]* annotation strings: E/I Ratio, Valsalva Ratio, 30:15 Ratio, "N possible premature beat(s);", operator notes with local clock times
[f64] test start, [f64] test end, [f64] test start (repeat), [f64] dt = 0.004 s, [u32] n, [u16 x n] EKG waveform (250 Hz)
[f64] t0, [u32] n_beats, [f32 x n_beats] beat-to-beat interval series (seconds)
[f64] t0, [f64] dt = 0.25 s, ([u32] n, [f32 x n]) x2 -> heart-rate series and breathing series (4 Hz)
[u32] 6, [f64 x 6] marker timestamps, then three 6-byte code arrays (semantics UNRESOLVED)
[f64] t0, [f64] dt = 4.0 s, ([u32] n, [f32 x n]) x11 -> spectral trend arrays (FRF, LFa/RFa power, percentages, ratio)
[f64] t0, [f64] dt = 4.0 s, [f64] 0.0033, [f64] 0.0066447, [u32] rows, [u32] cols = 150, [f32 x rows*cols] wavelet spectrogram

unresolved.item: phase (A-F) start/end boundaries and printed durations
unresolved.detail: The 6-entry marker block in the .ans holds 6 f64 timestamps plus three 6-byte code arrays, but the inter-marker intervals do not reproduce the durations printed in the Numerical Summary (e.g. Case 07 marker deltas 121.2/67.7/41.0/158.5/178.4 s vs printed 05:00/01:00/01:00/01:35/02:00/05:00). Phase windowing is therefore not yet reproducible from the binary alone.

unresolved.item: index-to-metric mapping of the 11 four-second trend arrays
unresolved.detail: Array 0 is FRF (range/scale match). Two arrays carry LFa- and RFa-like magnitudes, two arrays sum to 100 (percent split) and one is a ratio; the exact vendor order is not documented and was not confirmed field-by-field.

unresolved.item: the three 6-byte code arrays in the marker block
unresolved.detail: Non-printable/quasi-ASCII bytes that vary per case; likely marker type/quality codes. Not decoded.

Cuff BP values printed per phase were not located as an aligned numeric block in the .ans; candidate byte matches were coincidental hits inside waveform data. Treated as pdf_only pending vendor confirmation.
Printed MAP does not equal the textbook (SYS + 2*DIA)/3 in most rows (see validation checks); the vendor MAP formula is unknown and must not be reimplemented from assumption.

value: Patient presents with a high resting parasympathetic activity (RFa) relative to the resting sympathetic activity (LFa) as indicated by a low sympathovagal balance (SB < 0.4). Lifestyle changes, medications, or other therapies are recommended to restore and maintain balance. [For example, if Patient were on anticholinergics, it would be recommended that the dosage be titrated higher (or an additional cholinergic antagonist be introduced) to decrease the RFa and therefore, increase SB]
Low Normal sympathovagal balance (0.4 < SB < 1.0) may be too low for non-geriatric adults (less than age 65). Consider titrating therapy such that SB lies in the range from 1.0 - 2.0.

Alpha-Lipoic Acid (ALA: 200 to 600mg tid depending on severity), a non-prescription anti-oxidant that seems to be specific for nerves, has been known to slow the progression of autonomic neuropathy and can help restore and maintain autonomic balance [Prendergast, 2001]. NOTE: Alpha Lipoic Acid is known to lower resting BP [Magidenko, 2007; NutritionalReviews.Org, 2007].
If there is an intervention (therapy is added or changed), re-test in 3 months to check response to therapy (change). Otherwise retest in 6 months to follow up.
